newsitem.title: UK: Brown repeats UK unlikely to join EMU first wave.
newsitem.headline: Brown repeats UK unlikely to join EMU first wave.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchquer Gordon Brown said on Tuesday that Britain was unlikely to join in a single European currency in 1999.
"I've already said...as has the prime minister that it is highly unlikely we will join the first wave of EMU in 1999," Brown said at a news conference.

Brown also repeated that Britain's ultimate decision on whether to participate in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would be taken in the national economic interest and that policy was to keep options open.
Brown separately said on Tuesday that policy decisions by a new British monetary committee would be taken by majority vote.

"The decisions will be made by a vote of the committee with each member having one vote. If there is no majority, the Governor will have the final vote. The Treasury will have the right to be represented in a non-voting capacity," Brown said in a statement.
